analysis:
The two supplied units are head-text excerpts from docs/architecture/inference.md, lines 6368-6832: cluster memory-abort handling, MiMo V2.6 tensor parallel, MiMo placement, exact-quote placement and GLM tensor parallel. The changed ranges in file_changes cover only the onboarding stop text near line 453, which is not in these units. Even so, I read the supplied lines for security-relevant claims. The file is documentation only, with no code or configuration change, so I found no new attack surface or control regression.

Security-relevant statements: (1) The dev memory fault file (~/.darkbloom-dev/cluster-setup/memory-fault) is described as never read in a production install (lines 6463-6472). The doc says the file is deleted when a request starts. This claim is not verifiable from the docs, but it fits an existing test-only mechanism. (2) Sealed AES-256-GCM all-sums on the keyed JACCL data plane; a peer piece that fails to open fails the request. This fits the existing provider-to-peer cluster model. (3) GLM and MiMo prefix entries are partitioned per tenant (prefixScope, prefixDiskScope) and kept in the encrypted SSD tier. This matches T-041, which covers HMAC-keyed names, the 30-minute TTL and cacheSalt scoping. The doc adds nothing that loosens the TTL, the scope or the at-rest artifact. (4) Builds must match across the pair (peerBuildDiffers, rankBuildSHA256), and the load agreement binds the fingerprint, mode and data plane. (5) The media path caps encoded bytes at 32 MiB, and the leader bounds the ingest. These limits are DoS-relevant, and the doc states them.

Unverified contracts for later passes: the actual enforcement code for the production-install guard on ClusterMemoryFault, the SSD-tier scope binding for the GLM tensor-parallel prefix cache, and the 32 MiB media command bound (ClusterWorkerLimits.mediaCommandBytes). None of these sources was supplied. I treat them as coverage limits, not evidence of a defect.
